subject.title: Bug: Orphaned TaskFlows in `waiting` status permanently block agent heartbeats (requests-in-flight deadlock)

question: What should the permanent contract be for managed TaskFlow waits that stop receiving callbacks, and where should unattended recovery run?
rationale: Current source proves stale waits are only warned about, but the safe fix requires maintainer intent because existing plugin waits are durable and the heartbeat busy owner is not proven to be `flow_runs` alone.

options.title: Define Wait Abandonment And Runtime Recovery
options.body: Add an explicit deadline, abandonment signal, or proven orphan predicate and recover it in the gateway/runtime owner with upgrade and long-wait preservation proof.

options.title: Manual Repair Only
options.body: Keep stale waits as operator-visible audit findings and improve documented `tasks maintenance` or doctor guidance without claiming unattended heartbeat recovery.

options.title: Pause For Live Diagnosis
options.body: Hold implementation until a live reproduction identifies whether TaskFlow state, pending final delivery, active runs, or session lanes are the lasting busy resource.

recommendation.title: Define Wait Abandonment And Runtime Recovery
recommendation.body: Add an explicit deadline, abandonment signal, or proven orphan predicate and recover it in the gateway/runtime owner with upgrade and long-wait preservation proof.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history on TaskFlow maintenance and audit behavior, which is the central lifecycle surface needing a contract decision.
